svg.title: How voiceprint learns your voiceprint
svg.desc: Clean your text, pad sentences, slide a 4-word window, count what follows each context, blend long and short contexts with Kneser-Ney smoothing, compare your word use with general English, profile your style, and calibrate on held-out documents. Everything is saved to voice.vpi.
svg.text: Following one sentence through voiceprint build. Numbers are illustrative.
We then ship the **fix** to all 40

text.tspan: we then ship the fix to all

svg.text: Markup, code, links and numbers are stripped
or replaced, so only your wording is left.
Split into sentences, pad the start
Lowercased tokens, one sentence at a time.

text.tspan: markers mean even the first word has a

svg.text: context, so it learns how you open sentences.

text.tspan: teaches it how you end them.

svg.text: Each 3-word context → the word you wrote next.
The full 3-word context keeps raw counts. Shorter contexts count how many
different contexts a word completes (Kneser-Ney continuation counts).
Suggestions for a flagged word come from here.
your own counts, discounted weight left over for shorter contexts
Contexts you've used before mostly reuse your own counts. New contexts fall back
to shorter ones. Nothing is ever zero, so every word in a draft gets a score.
per 10k words. “really”: common in English, never
used by you → flagged when a draft uses it.
Measured per ~300-word chunk: mean and range.
How surprising your own unseen words are.
n-gram tables · slot index · your word counts · style profile · calibration · your sentences (for kwic)
